title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 100
paragraphs: The Eretrians, meanwhile, on being told that the Persian armament was sailing against them, asked the Athenians for help. The Athenians did not refuse — they sent as their supporters the four thousand who had been settled on the land of the wealthy Chalcidians. The Eretrians, however, had no solid plan of action. Though they had called for the Athenians, they were in fact divided between two minds: some proposed abandoning the city and fleeing to the heights of Euboea, while others, expecting to gain personally from the Persians, were preparing to hand the place over. Aeschines son of Nothon, one of the leading Eretrians, having learned how matters stood on both sides, told the Athenians who had come the whole state of affairs and begged them to depart for their own land so that they would not be destroyed as well. The Athenians took his advice and did just that.
